title: Differentially private federated learning with Byzantine-robust aggregation: A cross-domain framework for secure model training in banking and healthcare systems

C-a.quote: This composition, clip -> noise -> trimmed-mean, is what this paper calls DP-BR-FedAvg.
C-a.locator: Section III-E; the composition is stated as an ordered three-operation pipeline applied to every round, and TWO of the three operations carry a stated purpose of resisting corrupted updates, which is what Amendment 3 requires. (1) The clipping stage, PURPOSE QUOTED IN FULL BECAUSE THIS IS A PRIVACY-CLASS ROW (non-negotiable 12): "Clipping bounds the L2 sensitivity that the DP noise calibration depends on, and it caps how far a single Byzantine client's raw update can deviate before the robust aggregator is applied, improving the separation the aggregator can exploit." -- a single sentence stating a privacy purpose and a Byzantine purpose side by side. (2) The trimmed mean, "Rather than a simple mean, the server applies a coordinate-wise trimmed mean: for each coordinate j, the K", whose Byzantine purpose is restated in Section VI, "Against Byzantine clients, the trimmed-mean rule (Eq. 2) bounds the influence of any subset smaller than beta, following Yin et al. [4], though this bound degrades as sigma increases since added noise widens the spread of honest updates.". THE GAUSSIAN NOISE IS EXCISED UNDER AMENDMENT 3: its only stated purpose is the (epsilon, delta) guarantee against an honest-but-curious server, and the paper's own Figure 1 reading confirms the reading -- "Figure 1 plots test accuracy against communication round. Plain FedAvg and DP-FedAvg both plateau around 0.65-0.68 under the 25% Byzantine attack, well below the 0.84 clean reference, showing DP noise alone provides no protection against an aggregation-level attack. Byzantine-Robust FL converges fastest and reaches the highest accuracy (0.767) among attacked configurations. The proposed DP-BR-FedAvg tracks Byzantine-Robust FL early but drifts down to about 0.65, reflecting variance the Gaussian noise adds to the coordinatewise sorting trimmed mean depends on." says DP noise alone provides no protection against the attack. The code therefore rests on clipping plus trimmed mean, and does not depend on counting the DP layer

C-d.locator: Section V-C and Figure 4. GRADED-DOSE ROUTE (the coded route): sigma, the upstream DP noise scale, is swept from 0 to 1.8 with the DOWNSTREAM trimmed mean and the 25% Byzantine attack held fixed, an outcome under attack read at every setting, and TWO arms compared across the sweep (DP-FedAvg and DP-BR-FedAvg), so the sweep measures how the gap between a robust and a non-robust aggregator responds to the upstream stage's dose. The paper reports that gap NARROWING with dose and names the mechanism. INDEPENDENTLY SUFFICIENT COMPONENT-CONTRAST ROUTE: the baseline set is a complete 2x2 in the two mechanisms -- "dAvg: standard averaging, no privacy noise, no robust aggregation, under attack. •DP-FedAvg: clipping + Gaussian noise (Eq. 1, 4), simple averaging, under attack." and "•Byzantine-Robust FL: trimmed-mean aggregation (Eq. 2), no privacy noise, under attack. •DP-BR-FedAvg (proposed): clipping + noise + trimmed-mean aggregation, under attack. •FedAvg (no attack, reference): all clients honest, an upper-bound reference." -- so the arm with the trimmed mean and no privacy layer is exactly the upstream-removal contrast with the downstream held fixed, and the paper reads it off the composed outcome, "A Byzantine-robust aggregator with no privacy layer performs best in raw accuracy, quantifying the cost privacy imposes on robustness.". c_d_route records the graded-dose route under the tie-break rule stated in the coder note

A fourth, forward-looking attribution names a DIFFERENT downstream defense: "Trimmed mean is used as the default aggregator because it is coordinate-wise, cheap, and interacts more predictably with added Gaussian noise than Krum's pairwise selection, which is sensitive to the noise perturbing near-neighbor distance ranking."

coder_note:
THIS ROW IS THE STRONGEST EXTERNAL PRECEDENT IN THE FRAME AND A3 MUST CITE IT EXPLICITLY. Its subject is our subject, stated in its own words: "The results show that privacy and robustness mechanisms interact rather than simply add, and that system design for regulated, adversarial, cross-institutional settings needs to budget for that interaction.". The mechanism it gives is our attenuation channel, stated in the abstract's terms and again in the introduction: "clipping and noise injection, needed for privacy, change the statistics that a robust aggregator relies on to separate honest updates from adversarial ones, and a robust aggregator that discards or reweights updates https://thesesjournal.com | Nayak, 2024 | changes the sensitivity calculation the privacy guarantee depends on. This paper studies that interaction directly rather than assuming the two mechanisms compose without cost.". It runs a COMPLETE 2x2 in the two mechanisms under a fixed attack -- plain averaging, DP only, trimmed mean only, DP plus trimmed mean -- which is the first complete factorial in the frame; STAR-FL (2608.14861) has the same four cells scattered across three tables and never differences them, and PRoVeFL (2607.06612) is missing one margin entirely. It then sweeps the upstream dose (sigma from 0 to 1.8) against the fixed downstream rule and reports that the advantage of the robust aggregator NARROWS as the upstream dose grows, "This crossover is the central empirical finding: robustness and privacy do not simply add, and a tight privacy budget should be expected to erode the robustness guarantee.". An A4 sentence that implied nobody runs the identifying contrast would be false, and this row is why the plan's constraint on A4's wording was right.

WHAT WE ADD, AND IT HAS TO BE STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE OVERLAP IS REAL. (i) The paper varies the UPSTREAM stage only. Its downstream rule is trimmed mean in every arm, so no ordering across defenses can be produced, and it says as much about the quantity it did not measure: "Trimmed mean is used as the default aggregator because it is coordinate-wise, cheap, and interacts more predictably with added Gaussian noise than Krum's pairwise selection, which is sensitive to the noise perturbing near-neighbor distance ranking." -- an explicit claim that a DIFFERENT downstream mechanism would respond differently to the same upstream perturbation, offered as a design justification and never tested. That claim is exactly the content of Prop. prop:identification_full, asserted and unmeasured, and it is the single most on-point sentence the audit found. (ii) The evidence is a simulated dataset -- "Because raw banking transaction records and clinical records" -- one run per configuration, no seeds, no intervals, and no attack beyond corrupted-update Byzantine behavior (no backdoor, no ASR). (iii) The privacy accounting is explicitly loose, "Eq. (6) is used only for interpretability; a deployed system should use a tight numerical accountant [2] rather than this looser closed-form bound.", so the epsilon axis of the crossover figure is interpretive. (iv) The paper reports attenuation of a GAP, never a change in the ORDER of two defenses, and does not distinguish the two.

C-a = YES RESTS ON A DUAL-PURPOSE SENTENCE, THE FIRST IN THE FRAME WHERE BOTH PURPOSES ARE STATED IN THE SAME SENTENCE. "Clipping bounds the L2 sensitivity that the DP noise calibration depends on, and it caps how far a single Byzantine client's raw update can deviate before the robust aggregator is applied, improving the separation the aggregator can exploit." gives clipping a privacy purpose and a Byzantine purpose in one breath. Precedent is consistent in both directions and this row follows it: clipping COUNTED on FLAME, DeepSight, G2uardFL, DDFed and PQ-BRFL, each on a quoted poisoning-resistance purpose, and was EXCISED on Byz-Clip21-SGD2M (privacy sensitivity only) and SecureDyn-FL (numerical stability only). Here the defense half is quoted, so it counts. Dual-purpose single components now number four -- FedSAC's clustering (communication), Secure-CHG's CHG-Shapley (fairness), R2CFL's reputation (crowdsourcing incentives) and this clipping (privacy) -- and A5 should report that Amendment 3's purpose test resolves a component whose NAME misleads but does not resolve a component that genuinely does two jobs.

TIE-BREAK RULE FOR c_d_route, ADOPTED HERE AND APPLIED BACKWARD TO R2CFL, AND IT MUST BE DISCLOSED IN A5. Two rows now satisfy more than one C-d route at once. The rule is mechanical: if a graded upstream dose with an adversarial outcome at each setting exists, c_d_route records hyperparameter-sweep and the locator records the other route; otherwise it records the component contrast. The rule deliberately does NOT depend on which finding the paper calls central, because that is a judgement and both of this paper's routes are described as central in different places (the crossover in Section V-C, the no-privacy-layer comparison in the abstract). Under the rule, R2CFL (2608.08574) is hyperparameter-sweep as well, and its record was amended in the same session; Secure-CHG and FedSAC stay component-contrast because neither has a graded dose.
